issues.t: STI piston ringland failure
issues.sym: Blue or gray smoke from the exhaust, oil level dropping between changes, a rough idle or misfire on one cylinder, and sometimes a sudden loss of power.
issues.why: The 2.5L turbo engine in the STI uses cast pistons with a thin ledge (ringland) that holds the piston rings. Engine knock (detonation) from low-octane fuel, a lean mixture or an aggressive tune can crack that ledge, so the cylinder loses compression and burns oil.
issues.next: Use the premium fuel the car calls for and avoid untested tunes. If you see smoke or a misfire, stop hard driving and ask for a compression and leak-down test before more damage is done.

issues.t: WRX piston ringland failure
issues.sym: Rising oil use, blue smoke, a misfire on one cylinder or low compression on a test.
issues.why: The 2.5L turbo WRX engine shares the STI's weak point: the ledge in the piston that holds the rings can crack after repeated engine knock, especially on modified cars or with low-octane fuel.
issues.next: Track how much oil the engine uses. If it climbs, or a single-cylinder misfire code appears, have compression and leak-down tested to confirm before deciding on a repair.

issues.t: Rod bearing knock and spun bearings
issues.sym: A deep, rhythmic knock from low in the engine that gets louder with revs or load. The oil pressure light may flicker, and metal flakes can show up in the oil or filter.
issues.why: The bearings between the crankshaft and connecting rods in the 2.5L turbo engines can wear or spin, often after oil starvation or low oil. Subaru extended short-block coverage for some bearing failures on 2012-2014 WRX and 2012-2017 STI cars under bulletin 02-181-19.
issues.next: Stop driving if you hear a new deep knock, since a spun bearing can quickly destroy the engine. Check the oil level, get it towed for diagnosis, and ask a Subaru dealer whether the extended coverage still applies to your VIN.

issues.t: Excess sealant can reach the oil pickup
issues.sym: Usually nothing until the oil pressure warning comes on, or a new deep engine noise or turbo noise appears. Some owners found bits of cured gray sealant in the oil pan during service.
issues.why: Owners and independent shops have found extra RTV sealant squeezed out inside the oil pan of the 2.4L turbo engine. Pieces that break off can collect at the oil pickup screen and restrict oil flow. It is not shown to affect every car.
issues.next: If the oil pressure light comes on, shut the engine off as soon as it is safe and have it towed. If the oil pan is ever off for service, ask the shop to check the pickup screen for sealant debris.

issues.t: Carbon buildup on intake valves
issues.sym: Rough idle, stumbling on a cold start, misfire codes that come back after new plugs and coils, and a car that feels down on power.
issues.why: The 2.0L turbo engine sprays fuel straight into the cylinders, so fuel never washes the backs of the intake valves. Oily vapor from the crankcase vent bakes onto them over time. Subaru bulletin 02-193-24 describes a walnut-shell cleaning procedure.
issues.next: Have plugs, coils, injectors and vacuum leaks ruled out first. If carbon is confirmed, a walnut-blast cleaning fixes it; fuel additives cannot reach this area.

issues.t: Timing belt breaks or jumps a tooth
issues.sym: A squeal or chirp from the front of the engine, then the engine suddenly quits and cranks fast without starting.
issues.why: The older EJ boxer engines use a rubber timing belt with a 105,000-mile replacement interval. These are interference engines, so if the belt snaps or skips, pistons can hit the valves and wreck the engine.
issues.next: Check your records and replace the belt, tensioner, idlers and water pump on time. If it has already failed, do not keep cranking it; have the valves checked before anything else.

issues.t: Oil leaks at the front of the engine and AVCS faults
issues.sym: Oil dripping from the front of the engine, a burning oil smell, a rough idle or a check engine light for cam timing.
issues.why: On the 2.5L turbo engines, the seals around the variable valve timing (AVCS) cam sprockets can seep oil, and the oil control valves that run the system can clog or fail, especially if oil changes were stretched.
issues.next: Keep oil changes on schedule and look for drips. A cam timing code is usually a sticky oil control valve or low oil; a front seal leak should be fixed before it soaks the timing belt.

issues.t: Check engine light from the knock sensor
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with a knock sensor code. The car may feel slightly down on power.
issues.why: The knock sensor on these engines can fail or lose its connection. RepairPal notes the code often appears even when the sensor tests fine, so the wiring and mounting are worth checking first.
issues.next: Have the code read and the sensor wiring and connector inspected. The engine pulls back timing when knock readings are bad, so do not ignore it on a turbo car.

issues.t: Misfires from worn spark plug wires
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with misfire codes, and the engine may stumble under boost or idle roughly.
issues.why: Misfires on the early WRX were often traced to the spark plug wires, and Subaru released an improved wire set.
issues.next: Have the misfire code read and the plugs and wires checked. Replacing plugs and wires together is cheap insurance on a turbo engine.

issues.t: Clutch slips, shudders or wears out early
issues.sym: The clutch slips under load, shudders when pulling away, chirps or whirs when the pedal is pressed, or the pedal feels heavy or inconsistent.
issues.why: Manual 2015 to early 2018 cars had clutch, release bearing and pedal parts that Subaru later revised under bulletin 03-79-18. Clutch problems are the most-reported WRX complaint on CarComplaints, often around 14,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the clutch and its hydraulics inspected. If the clutch is replaced, ask for the updated parts from the bulletin, and check whether any warranty coverage applies.

issues.t: Five-speed manual grinds or pops out of gear
issues.sym: Grinding going into second or third, a gear that pops out, or a whine that rises with road speed.
issues.why: The five-speed manual in the regular WRX (not the STI) wears internally, especially on cars that were launched hard or given more power.
issues.next: Have the gearbox oil checked and the noise diagnosed. A clutch that does not fully release can feel similar, so rule that out first. Worn synchros or gears mean a rebuild or a used gearbox.

issues.t: STI six-speed grinds in fifth or sixth gear
issues.sym: Grinding when shifting into fifth or sixth gear.
issues.why: The synchronizers in the STI six-speed gearbox wear, so the gears do not match speeds smoothly before engaging.
issues.next: Try a fresh fluid change first. If grinding continues, plan for a synchro rebuild before gears are damaged.

issues.t: Judder or vibration when accelerating through turns
issues.sym: A shudder or vibration felt while accelerating in a turn.
issues.why: Subaru issued bulletin 16-136-22R with a temporary repair for this judder on the 2022 WRX.
issues.next: Mention the symptom and the bulletin number to the dealer; it should be handled under warranty.

issues.t: Fuel line can leak on cold starts (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell after starting the car in very cold weather.
issues.why: The steel fuel line can leak where it joins a rubber hose when it is very cold, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: Do not ignore a raw fuel smell. Check the VIN for recall 09V-468; the dealer replaces the fuel line for free.

issues.t: Turbo oil supply pipe can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Oil smell or smoke from the engine bay, or oil drips near the turbocharger.
issues.why: On some 2008 WRX cars the pipe feeding oil to the turbo was bent during assembly. Vibration can crack it and spray oil onto hot parts, a fire risk.
issues.next: Check the VIN for Subaru campaign WVF-16. The dealer inspects the pipe and adds a support bracket or replaces it for free.

issues.t: Turbo intake duct can crack (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls or loses boost, and the check engine light comes on.
issues.why: The air duct leading into the turbocharger on cars built April to October 2015 can crack, letting unmetered air in.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 16V-162 (Subaru WTA-62). The dealer checks the duct lot number and replaces it if needed.

issues.t: Low-pressure fuel pump can fail (recall)
issues.sym: The engine runs rough, stalls while driving or will not restart.
issues.why: The in-tank fuel pump can stop working.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 21V-587. The dealer replaces the pump for free.

issues.t: Crankcase vent (PCV) system fix (emissions recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing you notice; in some cases a check engine light.
issues.why: Subaru ran a voluntary emissions recall (WRB-22) on the 2.4L turbo engine for a problem in its crankcase ventilation (PCV) hose system.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to check the VIN for campaign WRB-22; the fix is free.

issues.t: Passenger airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning in normal driving. In a crash the passenger airbag inflator can burst and throw metal pieces.
issues.why: These cars used Takata passenger airbag inflators whose propellant breaks down after years of heat and humidity. Some cars needed a second replacement.
issues.next: Treat this as urgent. Check the VIN for recalls 20V-001/002/003 and the earlier 18V and 19V campaigns; the dealer replaces the inflator for free.

issues.t: Replacement airbag inflator may be fitted wrong (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom you can see.
issues.why: Passenger airbag inflators installed during an earlier recall on some 2004-2005 cars may have been fitted incorrectly.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 23V-076 even if the airbag was already replaced once.

issues.t: Brake lines can rust through (recall)
issues.sym: A soft or sinking brake pedal, or brake fluid on the ground near the rear of the car.
issues.why: In salt-belt states, salty water splashes through a gap by the fuel tank guard and corrodes the brake lines until they leak. The first fix (14V-311) was not enough, so a follow-up recall (14V-830) added more rust protection.
issues.next: Check the VIN for both recalls. A soft pedal or leaking fluid means the car should not be driven until it is inspected.

issues.t: Brake light switch can fail (recall)
issues.sym: Brake lights stop working. On some cars the push-button start or shifting out of Park also stops working.
issues.why: Contamination inside the brake light switch can stop it from making contact.
issues.next: Ask someone to check your brake lights. Check the VIN for recall 19V-149; the dealer replaces the switch for free.

issues.t: Replacement ignition switch can slip out of Run (recall)
issues.sym: The engine suddenly shuts off while driving, along with power steering and brake assist.
issues.why: A replacement-part ignition switch fitted to some cars has a spring that can break, so the switch moves to accessory.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 19V-297. The dealer inspects the switch and replaces it if needed.

issues.t: Backup light switch can corrode (recall)
issues.sym: The reverse lights do not come on and the rearview camera image does not appear when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: The switch on the transmission that signals reverse gear can corrode and stop working.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 22V-522. The dealer replaces the switch if needed.

issues.t: Trunk subwoofer wiring can short (recall)
issues.sym: The factory subwoofer cuts out, or there is a burning smell from the trunk.
issues.why: On cars with the optional subwoofer, cargo can push its wiring against the metal frame until it shorts and overheats.
issues.next: Keep heavy items away from the subwoofer and check the VIN for recall 17V-625 (Subaru WTQ-76).

issues.t: Brake switch fault can disable EyeSight braking (recall)
issues.sym: Pre-collision braking may not work, sometimes with no warning.
issues.why: On EyeSight cars built around March 2015, a failed brake light switch can switch off automatic emergency braking.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 15V-366. The dealer reprograms the driver assist system for free.

issues.t: Front driveshaft joint can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Clicking or clunking from the front when turning, then possibly a sudden loss of drive power. A parked car could roll if the parking brake is not set.
issues.why: The outer joint on the front driveshafts can crack and break.
issues.next: Use the parking brake every time you park and check the VIN for recall 23V-754. The dealer inspects and replaces the driveshafts for free.

issues.t: Battery drains when the car sits
issues.sym: The car will not start after sitting for a few days, or the battery dies early.
issues.why: A class-action lawsuit claimed the electrical system keeps drawing power after shutdown. Subaru denied it, but a 2023 settlement extended coverage for some battery failures.
issues.next: Have the battery and parasitic draw tested, keep receipts, and ask a dealer whether the settlement coverage applies to your car.

issues.t: Windshield cracks easily
issues.sym: A crack appears in the windshield with little or no impact, often at low mileage.
issues.why: Several owners of the 2014 WRX report windshields that crack easily, at an average of about 13,000 miles.
issues.next: Check whether your insurance covers glass. Ask the dealer for a goodwill replacement if it happens very early.

issues.t: Check engine light for the EVAP purge valve
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P04AE.
issues.why: The engine computer can wrongly flag the fuel vapor purge valve as stuck open. Subaru bulletin 09-114-23 adds new engine computer software.
issues.next: Have the code read and ask the dealer about bulletin 09-114-23. It should be covered by warranty.

issues.t: Rattle or flutter from a cracked front exhaust pipe
issues.sym: A rattling or fluttering sound from under the car.
issues.why: The front exhaust pipe can crack. Subaru changed its design and described the fix in bulletin 09-106-23R.
issues.next: Have the exhaust inspected under the car and mention the bulletin.

issues.t: Touchscreen flashes, freezes or shuts off
issues.sym: The lower touchscreen flashes, stops responding to touch or goes dark.
issues.why: Subaru has several bulletins for the Denso head unit, including 15-273-20 for a flashing or unresponsive lower display and software updates for it.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to check for head unit software updates before replacing parts.

issues.t: Popping or clicking from the front struts in turns
issues.sym: A pop or click from the front suspension during slow, tight turns or at full steering lock.
issues.why: Owners have traced the noise to the front strut mount bearings. Subaru also issued a 2025 suspension bulletin (05-92-25) for this model year.
issues.next: Have the strut mounts checked and ask the dealer about the suspension bulletin.

issues.t: Driver-assist false warnings or cruise control dropouts
issues.sym: Forward collision warnings with nothing in the way, or adaptive cruise and lane warnings acting up.
issues.why: Owners filed complaints about false forward collision warnings on 2024 cars, and Subaru issued bulletin 07-226-24R covering adaptive cruise and lane departure warning concerns on 2023 cars.
issues.next: Keep the windshield in front of the EyeSight cameras clean and ask the dealer to check for the bulletin and camera calibration.

issues.t: Satellite radio ads pop up on the screen while driving
issues.sym: A full-screen SiriusXM ad appears over the navigation map or audio controls while driving and has to be dismissed.
issues.why: Several owners have reported these pop-up messages to NHTSA. Dealers say there is no fix, since they come from the infotainment software.
issues.next: Pull over before dismissing messages. You can report it to Subaru and NHTSA; check for infotainment software updates.
